ai.title: Backend Docker deployment, build scripts, and system prompt update
ai.summary: Added backend/Dockerfile and backend/deploy.sh to containerize and push the backend service to gcr.io/manicode-430317/manicode-backend. Updated backend/package.json and common/package.json with composite TypeScript build scripts (prebuild, postbuild, clean) and renamed backend/src/openai.ts to backend/src/openai-api.ts. Modified backend/src/system-prompt.ts to instruct the agent to skip editing files if contents are already correct, preventing redundant writes.

eli5.text: The backend service can now be packaged and deployed automatically using containerization tools, making it easier to update and manage. When you deploy, it will bundle the backend code and its shared components together, build them, and push the packaged version to a hosting platform. Additionally, the assistant now checks if a file already has the correct content before rewriting it, avoiding unnecessary changes. These improvements streamline the deployment process and reduce redundant work.

ai.title: Add GCP VM deploy script, update main prompt with scrapewebpage tool
ai.summary: backend/deploy.sh expanded from bare `yarn build` and `docker build` into full GCP deployment pipeline: Docker image build, GCR push, firewall rule creation, and `gcloud compute instances create-with-container` on e2-micro VM in us-east4-a. backend/src/main-prompt.ts adds instruction to invoke `scrape_web_page` tool when user provides URL, before `read_files` request. Scope internal, repo-level only.

eli5.text: You can now spin up a hosted version of the backend on Google Cloud with a single command, rather than having to build the Docker image and start the container by hand. The deployment script builds the image, pushes it to Google's container storage, opens the needed firewall port, and launches a small cloud server (e2-micro) in the us-east4-a region running that container. Separately, the assistant's instructions were updated so that when you paste a web address instead of a file, it will fetch and read that webpage before looking at any local files. Both pieces landed in the backend area and are live today.
